meta_title: MijiaBar — Mi Home in your Mac menu bar
meta_description: MijiaBar is a free, open-source menu bar app for Xiaomi Mi Home on macOS. Control air conditioners, lights, fans and cameras in a click, and let AI agents help — safely.
hero_title:
Your Mi Home.
Right in the menu bar.
hero_sub: Air conditioners, lights, fans and cameras — one click away, without reaching for your phone.
hero_fine: Free and open source|macOS 14 or later|Apple silicon and Intel
not_mac: MijiaBar is a Mac app. Open this page on your Mac to download it.
alt_list: MijiaBar open from the menu bar, with two air conditioners in Favorites and the other devices grouped by room.
devices_title: Every device looks and feels like the real thing.
devices_lead: Each kind of device has its own page, with an illustration that changes as the device does. Airflow follows the fan speed, bulbs glow at their color temperature, and plugs show current flowing.
g_ac: Air conditioners. Drag to set the temperature. Mode, fan speed and swing are one click each.
g_light: Lights. Brightness and color temperature, with a bulb that glows to match.
g_fan: Fans. The blades turn at the speed you set, and coast to a stop when you switch off.
g_plug: Smart plugs. See how much power is being drawn right now.
g_heat: Heating. Colors follow the mode — cool blue for cooling, warm orange for heating.
alt_ac: Air conditioner page: cooling, target temperature 24 degrees, with mode, fan speed and swing controls.
alt_light: Light page with brightness and color temperature controls.
alt_plug: Smart plug page showing the current power draw.
alt_heat: Air conditioner page in heating mode, tinted orange.
lineup_title: One menu for the whole home.
lineup_lead: From air conditioners to printers, the devices you use most get pages of their own. Everything else in Mi Home still works — MijiaBar builds its controls from the device's MIoT spec.
cam_title: Check the camera without leaving the menu bar.
cam_lead: Live video plays right inside the device card. Pop it out into its own window when you want a closer look.
cam_p1_d: The stream starts when you open it and stays on this Mac.
cam_p2_d: Video is never saved, and your keys stay in the Keychain.
cam_p3_d: The agent interface has no access to camera video.
cam_note: Live view works when your Mac is on your home network.
alt_camera: Camera page playing live video, with a button to stop and a night mode setting.
hood_title: Quick, private and made for everyone.
t_path_t: Cloud or local network — whichever gets through.
t_path_d: MijiaBar reaches devices through the Xiaomi cloud and falls back to your local network when it has to. Away from home it skips the wait, and every device shows which path it took.
t_qr_d: Scan the code with the Mi Home app — no password to type. Your session stays in the macOS Keychain.
t_qr_r: Servers in Mainland China, Europe, the United States, Russia, Singapore and India.
t_keys_d: Open the menu and do everything without touching the trackpad.
t_a11y_d: VoiceOver labels on every control, and Reduce Motion is respected throughout.
t_theme_d: Follows your Mac's appearance, down to every illustration.
t_update_d: Signed updates install from inside the app. Every release is notarized by Apple.
agent_title: Let your AI agent run the house. On your terms.
agent_lead: MijiaBar comes with a command-line tool and an MCP server. Paste one message into Claude Code, Codex or Cursor and the agent sets itself up.
prompt_where: This assumes MijiaBar is in Applications. The same message, with your path filled in, is in Settings → Agent interface.
perm_title: You decide what it can do.
perm_read_d: List devices and read their state.
perm_allow_d: Control only the devices you pick.
perm_confirm: Confirm every write — each change waits for your OK in a dialog on your Mac.
start_title: Up and running in a minute.
s1_d: Open the disk image and drag MijiaBar into Applications.
s2_d: Click the house in the menu bar, choose your region, and scan the code with the Mi Home app.
s3_d: When macOS asks the first time you control a device, click Allow so MijiaBar can reach it directly.
alt_login: MijiaBar sign-in screen with a QR code to scan with the Mi Home app.
a1: A Mac with macOS 14 Sonoma or later — Apple silicon or Intel — and a Xiaomi account with devices in the Mi Home app.
a2: No. It's an independent open-source project. It uses the same cloud API as the Mi Home app, plus the miIO protocol on your local network.
a3: Every release is signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple. The source code is public on GitHub under the MIT license.
q4: Where does my account information go?
a4: You sign in by scanning a QR code, so there's no password to type. Your session is stored in the macOS Keychain and is only sent to Xiaomi.
q5: Does it work outside mainland China?
a5: Yes. Choose your Mi Home server when you sign in: Mainland China, Europe, United States, Russia, Singapore or India.
q6: Can I use it away from home?
a6: Yes. Controls go through the Xiaomi cloud when your Mac isn't on your home network. Live camera view needs your home network.
a7: Most likely. Devices without a page of their own still get controls built from their MIoT spec. If something doesn't work, let us know on GitHub.
a8: From version 0.1.9 on, MijiaBar checks for updates by itself, and you can check any time in Settings. If you have 0.1.8 or earlier, download the latest version once.
final_title: Put your home in the menu bar.
foot_disclaimer: MijiaBar is an independent open-source project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Xiaomi. Xiaomi and Mi Home are trademarks of their respective owners.
